definitions.title: The shared shelf
definitions.instructions: Read the complete passage, then answer each question. You may consult the passage.
definitions.content: At a neighborhood workshop, Lina placed a box of spare pencils beside the door. Visitors could take one and leave another when they had a spare. On the first day, the box emptied before lunch. Lina moved it beside the sign-in desk and added a note asking people to return unused pencils. By Friday, there were enough pencils for the next workshop. The note did not ask for money; it made the shared arrangement easier to understand.

options: To make the arrangement visible at sign-in

definitions.title: A cooler courtyard
definitions.instructions: Read the complete passage, then answer each question. You may consult the passage.
definitions.content: A school courtyard became very hot at midday. Amir suggested planting trees, but trees would need years to provide shade. The team first installed a removable cloth canopy. They checked temperatures in two equally sunny corners at noon for a week, covering only one corner. The covered corner stayed cooler. They kept the canopy for the summer and planted trees nearby for future shade. The quick solution and the slower solution served different time scales.

options: They help at different time scales

definitions.title: The repair notebook
definitions.instructions: Read the complete passage, then answer each question. You may consult the passage.
definitions.content: At a small repair cafe, volunteers often solved the same lamp fault more than once. Sara started a notebook with a symptom, the test used, and the repair that worked. She left space for cases where a repair failed. A later volunteer discovered that two lamps with the same symptom needed different repairs. Instead of replacing the first entry, he added the second case. The notebook became useful because it kept both the successful repairs and the limits of each explanation.
